ad_library.summary: At least 5 live Meta ads on the SunSolarhyd page (page ID 1056719797535626) on 2026-11-21, running since 22 Oct 2026 with two fresh creatives on 21 Nov 2026 (6 hrs live at read). The page sells a price ladder - 3 kW Rs.1,31,999, 4 kW Rs.1,71,999, 5 kW Rs.2,18,999 - every rung presented as 'subsidy included' with Rs.0 down payment, '30 Years Warranty', free site visit and Adani / Waaree panels. Every ad clicks to a Facebook lead form. There is no website: sunsolarpowersolutions.in does not resolve, so no site audit was run.

funnel.destination: Facebook lead form (FB.ME) - 'Get offer' on every ad
funnel.meaning: There is no website and no landing page anywhere in the funnel: every click on a Rs.1.3-2.2 lakh offer ends in a Facebook lead form. The buyer cannot check the company, the warranty terms or the address before handing over a phone number, and nothing can be retargeted or followed up outside the Meta inbox.

findings: There is no website at all - sunsolarpowersolutions.in returns DNS NXDOMAIN - yet the ads quote a full price ladder up to Rs.2,18,999. A buyer cannot check the firm, the warranty exclusions or the address anywhere before submitting a phone number.

The page prints its own phone number two different ways inside the same offer set: '+91 98666 02001' in the 3 kW and 4 kW ads, '+91 98666 20001' in the 5 kW ad. One of the two is wrong on a lakh-scale purchase, and nobody can tell which from outside.

'30 Years Warranty' is stated with no qualifier in every ad - no distinction between the module's performance warranty and the inverter, structure or workmanship, which is where the buyer's real risk sits.

The 3 kW creative is re-used verbatim for Hyderabad (Oct 22) and Ananthapur (Oct 23) - only the first word changes, and the Ananthapur version still carries #Hyderabad in its hashtags - so the same Rs.1,31,999 is quoted across two different markets with no stated exclusions and a hashtag pointing at the wrong city.

Every offer is presented as a net price - the 5 kW ad runs the sum out loud, 'Original Price Rs.2,96,999 - Government Subsidy Rs.78,000 = Your Final Price Rs.2,18,999' - but no ad says whether SunSolar nets that Rs.78,000 into the invoice or whether the buyer pays in full and waits for the subsidy to be credited after commissioning. On a Rs.2.19 lakh purchase that is the difference between arranging Rs.2.19 lakh and arranging Rs.2.97 lakh, and the ads never say which.
'0 Down Payment' and 'Easy EMI Available' are stated without a lender, a tenure, a rate or a monthly figure anywhere in the ad set, so the single number a homeowner actually budgets cannot be found.
Four of the five ads click to a lead form with no landing page, no UTM and no distinct offer tracking, so the 3 kW, 4 kW and 5 kW creatives cannot be compared against each other.
next_steps: Register one domain and put a single page on it

A one-page site with the price ladder, the Rs.78,000 subsidy mechanics, the warranty split (module / inverter / workmanship), the Kokapet office address and a form with a Meta Pixel. Without it there is nothing to verify and nothing to retarget.
Fix the phone number to one correct format
The page currently prints 98666 02001 and 98666 20001 in the same campaign. Pick the live one, use it everywhere, and put it on the landing page as a tel: link.
Split the warranty claim into its three parts

'30 Years Warranty' with no qualifier reads as a warranty on the whole system. State module performance, inverter and workmanship separately - it is the fastest way to look more credible than the competitor making the same claim.
Say how the Rs.78,000 actually reaches the buyer

State plainly that the subsidy is credited to the customer after commissioning, and what the buyer pays up front. Every ad currently presents a net price that may not be the amount payable at booking.
Put one EMI figure against each kW size
'Easy EMI Available' is in all five ads and no ad gives a tenure or a monthly amount. One line - 3 kW, Rs.X/month, Y years - answers the question the lead form is asking the buyer to ask.
Use the Ananthapur variant as a lesson, not a template
Re-running the Hyderabad creative with only the city swapped means neither market gets a locally priced, locally evidenced offer.

promise_gap.site: There is no site and no warranty document anywhere, so a buyer cannot tell whether this covers the module only, the inverter, the structure or the workmanship.

ads_audit.methodology: Control review follows the claude-ads Meta Ads audit catalog (github.com/vamsy16/claude-ads, ads/references/meta-audit.md). Each control is graded only where public evidence establishes it - Ad Library ad data and the lead's own landing page. Controls that require Ads Manager access (bidding, budgets, audiences, learning phase, EMQ, CAPI status) are marked unknown on purpose: they cannot be verified from outside the account and are never guessed.
